title: Trade suggestions returns zero suggestions for 8 of 12 live teams, with no diagnosis in the payload
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: suggestions.py produces 'roster-aware trade suggestions (sell-high, buy-low, consolidation, upgrades)' gated on BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER=150.
observed: Posting each of the 12 real Sleeper rosters (plus all 12 as league_rosters) returns totalSuggestions=0 for Ed, Ty, Collin, Roy, Joey, Kich, jstuedle and Blaine. Of the 4 that return anything, 3 return sellHigh only. positionalUpgrades is 0 for all 12 teams. Cause: the single-population top-150 board gate leaves rosterMatched at 3-21 of the 44-58 players actually rostered (jstuedle 3/44, Blaine 5/53), so the engine analyses 5-36% of the roster it was handed. metadata reports rosterMatched/rosterProvided but the payload carries no error, warning or 'insufficient coverage' note.

reproduction.command:
SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/full.json; python - <<'EOF'
import json,subprocess
d=json.load(open('/tmp/full.json')); T=d['sleeper']['teams']
lr=[{'team_name':t['name'],'players':t['players']} for t in T]
for t in T:
    p=subprocess.run(['curl','-s','-b','/tmp/c.txt','-X','POST','http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/suggestions','-H','Content-Type: application/json','-d',json.dumps({'roster':t['players'],'league_rosters':lr})],capture_output=True)
    r=json.loads(p.stdout); print(t['name'], r['totalSuggestions'], r['metadata']['rosterMatched'],'/',r['metadata']['rosterProvided'])
EOF
reproduction.expected: every team receives at least one actionable suggestion, or an explicit reason why not
reproduction.actual: 8/12 return {sellHigh:[],buyLow:[],consolidation:[],positionalUpgrades:[],totalSuggestions:0} with HTTP 200 and no warning field

userImpact: A user on /trade asking for trade ideas is told, silently, that there are none. Two thirds of the league concludes the feature is broken or that their roster has no trades available; neither is true — the engine simply never looked at 79-93% of their roster.

priorFinding.note: Prior said 7 of 12; I measure 8 of 12 with league_rosters supplied. PRIOR-A14-F19 ('no refuses-to-answer path') is also confirmed by the same run — the empty payload carries no diagnosis.

whatWorks: metadata.rosterMatched / rosterProvided are honestly stamped, so the shortfall is at least measurable from the payload. starter_needs_for_league correctly derives per-league lineups (QB2/RB3/WR4/TE2/DL3/LB3/DB3 for dynasty_main).
rootCause: build_asset_pool_from_contract ranks ALL asset classes in one population and cuts at 150 (suggestions.py:646-651). Offense dominates the top of a 0-9999 board, so a 58-man roster in a 58-slot IDP league resolves to a handful of eligible assets.
requiredRepair: Gate per asset class / per position family (as finder.py already does per market), or make the gate roster-relative. Failing that, emit an explicit 'coverage insufficient' warning naming rosterMatched/rosterProvided so an empty feed reads as 'not measured', never 'nothing available'.
dependencies: W09-F004 (DB exclusion) is the same root cause seen from the position axis.

title: Every trade the arbitrage finder returns is a 1-for-2; 1-for-1 candidates exist but rank 2,159th and 2-for-1 never qualifies at all
claimUnderTest: finder.py generates three package shapes (_generate_1for1, _generate_2for1, _generate_1for2) and ranks them together by arbitrage_score.
observed: 480 returned trades across all 12 teams: 480 are '1-for-2'. Zero 1-for-1, zero 2-for-1. Running find_trades for Jason with max_results=100000 yields 5,562 qualified trades — 5,399 1-for-2, 163 1-for-1, and ZERO 2-for-1 — and the first 1-for-1 appears at rank 2,159. The scoring function is the cause: board_gain_norm = board_delta / give_model divides by the give side only, so shrinking the give side to one asset inflates the dominant term (f_board_edge = board_gain_norm*50) without bound, while the entire counterweight is f_simplicity = -(pkg_size-2)*3 = -3.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.trade import finder as F;from collections import Counter;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));T=d['sleeper']['teams'];r=F.find_trades(d['players'],'Jason',[t['name'] for t in T if t['name']!='Jason'],T,max_results=100000,ktc_top_n=150,contract=d);print(Counter(x['packageSize'] for x in r['trades']));print('first 1-for-1 at rank',[i for i,x in enumerate(r['trades']) if x['packageSize']=='1-for-1'][0]+1)"
reproduction.expected: a mix of shapes in the top 40

numericProof.formula: share of returned trades with packageSize == '1-for-2' = returned1for2 / returnedTotal

userImpact: /arbitrage presents itself as a general trade finder. A user never sees a straight player-for-player swap or a consolidation offer, only 'give one good player, get two lesser ones' — the single shape that is hardest to get accepted and that structurally worsens roster-spot pressure in a 58-slot league.

priorFinding.note: Prior measured 98% of output in the 1-for-N direction; the live measurement is 100% of returned output (480/480) and 97.1% of qualified output (5399/5562). The 2-for-1 direction that the guards WERE written for produces zero qualifying trades, so those guards are dead in production.

whatWorks: _deduplicate correctly collapses same-asset permutations; the multi-for-one guards (MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO, ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO, PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT) are correctly implemented — they just guard a direction that never survives the output filter.
rootCause: The normalizer in board_gain_norm is give_model, not (give_model+recv_model)/2 or max(); combined with a flat -3 simplicity penalty this makes score monotonically increasing in receive-side count.
requiredRepair: Normalize board_delta against the larger of the two sides (or their mean), and/or reserve slots per package shape in the returned list so each shape gets representation. Either fix must be re-measured against the shape distribution above.

title: Draft picks can never appear in a trade-finder or trade-suggestion result: both engines resolve rosters from sleeper.teams[].players, which contains zero picks
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'offense + picks -> ktcSfTep' — picks are a first-class asset class in the finder's per-market gate, and build_asset_pool explicitly classifies is_pick and routes picks to the KTC board.
observed: 25 picks survive the top-150 offense-market gate and sit in the finder's asset pool. Zero picks appear in any of the 480 returned trades, for any of the 12 teams. _resolve_roster (finder.py:621) reads only t['players'] from the Sleeper team dict; that list contains 0 pick entries on all 12 teams. The picks the league owns live in the SIBLING keys t['picks'] (e.g. ['2026 1st','2026 2nd',...]) and t['pickDetails'], which neither engine reads. /api/trade/suggestions has the same shape: the route passes body['roster'] straight through, and the /trade page sources it from the same players list.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.trade import finder as F;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));t=d['sleeper']['teams'][0];print('pick-like entries in t[players]:',[p for p in t['players'] if p.startswith('20')]);print('t[picks]:',t['picks'][:6]);bv=F.board_values_from_contract(d);po=F.positions_from_contract(d);pool=F.build_asset_pool(d['players'],market_top_n=150,board_values=bv,positions=po);print('picks in gated pool:',sum(1 for a in pool if a.is_pick))"
reproduction.expected: picks tradeable, since 25 of them clear the market gate
reproduction.actual: pick-like entries in t[players]: []; t[picks]: ['2026 1st','2026 2nd','2026 3rd','2026 4th','2026 5th','2026 6th']; picks in gated pool: 25

userImpact: Player-plus-pick and pick-for-player are the two most common real dynasty trade shapes. A user on /arbitrage is shown a search that structurally cannot propose either, with nothing saying so — and the 18 picks occupying the top-150 offense-market gate displace 18 real players that COULD have been traded.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index. Prior A14 covered the finder's IDP blindness but not its pick blindness.

whatWorks: build_asset_pool's pick classification (is_pick, EXCLUDED_POSITIONS, market routing) is correct — 25 picks are priced and ranked. The break is purely in roster resolution.
rootCause: _resolve_roster reads one of the three asset-bearing keys on the Sleeper team dict.
requiredRepair: Extend _resolve_roster to concatenate t['players'] with t['picks'] (normalising pickDetails labels to the contract's pick row names via contract['pickAliases']), and pass picks through the suggestions route the same way. Also exclude picks from the offense-market top-N population, or rank them as their own market, so they stop displacing players from the gate.
dependencies: Requires pick-name alias resolution — the contract keys picks as '2026 Pick 1.01'/'2027 Early 1st' while Sleeper labels them '2026 1st'.

title: No defensive back is eligible for any trade suggestion: the best DB on the board ranks 167th, past the top-150 gate, in a league that starts three of them
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: suggestions.py gates on BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER (150) against 'our blended board — display_value order, covers every asset class'. The route derives starter_needs including DB:3.
observed: The 150-asset pool contains 41 WR, 28 QB, 26 RB, 23 PICK, 18 TE, 7 DL, 7 LB and ZERO DB. The board carries 96 DBs; the highest, Caleb Downs (3159), sits at overall rank 167 — 17 places past the cut, against a rank-150 cutoff value of 3259. dynasty_main starts 3 DB per team (36 league-wide starting DB slots) and the engine's own starterNeeds echo 'DB: 3'. Consequently every suggestion generated for the one team that gets a full feed (Brent) targets an LB or a QB; the receive-side position histogram over all 9 of its suggestions is {LB: 8, QB: 1}.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from collections import Counter;from src.trade.suggestions import build_asset_pool_from_contract as B;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));p=B(d,ktc_top_n=150);print(Counter(x.position for x in p));f=B(d,ktc_top_n=0);dbs=sorted([x for x in f if x.position=='DB'],key=lambda z:-z.display_value);print('total DBs on board',len(dbs),'best',dbs[0].name,dbs[0].display_value,'rank',dbs[0].board_rank);print('rank-150 cutoff value',sorted(f,key=lambda z:-z.display_value)[149].display_value)"
reproduction.expected: DB representation proportional to its 3 starting slots
reproduction.actual: Counter has no 'DB' key; total DBs on board 96, best Caleb Downs 3159 at rank 167; rank-150 cutoff value 3259

userImpact: A manager whose actual weakness is at DB is told their roster needs DB (starterNeeds says so) and is then offered zero DB targets — and no message explains that DBs were excluded rather than considered and rejected.

priorFinding.note: Same root cause as the zero-suggestion finding, measured on the position axis instead of the roster-coverage axis. Not separately stated in the prior index.

whatWorks: finder.py already solved exactly this problem by ranking each market's own population from 1 (MARKET_TOP_N_FILTER) — the pattern to copy exists in the sibling module.
rootCause: One global top-N cut over a value scale on which offense occupies the entire top of the board.
requiredRepair: Gate per position family (or per asset class) inside build_asset_pool_from_contract, mirroring finder.py's per-market grouping, and stamp the per-family counts in metadata so the composition is visible.

title: Monte Carlo uncertainty is a hard-coded flat +/-15% band on zero live rows, and the 9999 clamp makes it understate an elite asset by 5.07%
claimUnderTest: monte_carlo.py module docstring: 'Given side-A and side-B as lists of players, each with a valueBand from Phase 4 (p10, p50, p90)... Depends on: Phase 4 confidence intervals'. build_trade_player: 'Prefers the Phase 4 valueBand dict; falls back to +/-15% band'.
observed: 0 of 1,092 playersArray rows carry a valueBand, so the fallback IS the production path for every asset — every player, pick and defender is drawn from an identical +/-15% triangle regardless of whether the board blended 1 source or 14 (effectiveSourceRanks ranges 0-14 across the contract). The frontend synthesizes the same +/-15% band client-side. Worse, _shifted() clamps to 9999 while the +15% leg is not, so for a top-of-board asset the upper half of the band is truncated and the sampled mean falls BELOW the board value: Brock Bowers (rankDerivedValue 9947) simulates at sideAMean 9441.9. No convergence diagnostic, standard error, confidence interval or seed echo is returned; ten identical calls give winProbA 0.0001-0.0003 and meanDelta -4455.2 to -4439.3.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print('rows with valueBand:',sum(1 for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('valueBand')),'of',len(d['playersArray']))" ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sideA":[{"name":"Brock Bowers","rankDerivedValue":9947,"pos":"TE","team":"LV"}],"sideB":[{"name":"Jonathan Taylor","rankDerivedValue":6431,"pos":"RB","team":"IND"},{"name":"Patrick Mahomes","rankDerivedValue":7461,"pos":"QB","team":"KC"}]}' | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["sideAMean"], r["nSims"])'
reproduction.expected: sideAMean == 9947 (the board value the user is shown)

numericProof.formula: E[draw] = sum over segments of ((lo+hi)/2)*weight, using the piecewise-linear _triangular_draw quantile map

userImpact: On /trade the MC panel says 'Side B came out ahead in 100% of 20,000 simulations'. That number is produced from an invented, uniform uncertainty and a mean that is 5% low for exactly the elite assets a trade usually hinges on. A user rejects an even trade because the simulator's fabricated distribution says it is not close.

priorFinding.note: Also confirms PRIOR-A09-F03 and PRIOR-A10-F02, which state the same defect from the constants and documentation angles. New here is the 9999-clamp bias: the fabricated band is not merely uninformative, it is directionally WRONG at the top of the board, understating the board value by 504 points (5.07%) with an analytic derivation that matches the live sideAMean to 1.1 points.

whatWorks: The direction-symmetrization is real and effective (symmetryCheck.drift 0.0001, enforced true), the labelHint/disclaimer contract fields ARE returned by the backend, and run-to-run variance is genuinely small (meanDelta sd 5.1 on a magnitude of 4,447 over 10 runs at 100k sims) — the estimator is stable, it is just estimating a fabricated quantity.
rootCause: The band producer (src/canonical/confidence_intervals) never stamps valueBand onto contract rows, so the documented input does not exist on any live row; the fallback was written as a degradation path and became the only path.
requiredRepair: Either stamp valueBand from the data the contract already carries (effectiveSourceRanks spread / sourceSpread / confidenceBucket are all present per row), or stop reporting a win probability and report the point delta only. At minimum, clamp p50 and p90 consistently so the sampled mean equals the displayed board value, and return a convergence statistic (MC standard error on winProbA) so the reader can tell a stable 0.50 from a noisy one.
dependencies: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py has no producer wired into the contract build.

title: The leagueAdjusted valuation lens is a silent no-op on every all-offense trade in /api/trade/simulate and /api/trade/finder, while the response still stamps valuationMode: leagueAdjusted
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'No engine knows the feature exists, because every engine reads exactly one value — rankDerivedValue' and 'Every response stamps valuationMode — including "market". "This is the market board" and "this field is missing" must not read the same.'
observed: overlay.adjusted_rows multiplies ONLY row['rankDerivedValue'] by the position factor. But both trade_simulator._resolve_asset and finder._score_trade prefer offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue when the trade contains no IDP asset — a field the overlay never touches. A Bowers-for-(Taylor+Mahomes) simulate call returns equity 4004 and per-player values 9950/6472/7482 under BOTH valuationMode=market and valuationMode=leagueAdjusted, and stamps 'leagueAdjusted' on the second. Substituting an IDP asset makes the lens visible immediately (Bowers 9947->10062, Hutchinson 6362->6984), proving the plumbing works and only the offense-only field is missed.

reproduction.command: for M in market leagueAdjusted; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"teamName\":\"Jason\",\"playersOut\":[\"Brock Bowers\"],\"playersIn\":[\"Jonathan Taylor\",\"Patrick Mahomes\"],\"valuationMode\":\"$M\"}" | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["valuationMode"], r["equity"], [(x["name"],x["value"]) for x in r["sending"]+r["receiving"]])'; done
reproduction.expected: equity differs between the two modes

userImpact: A user who switches the board to 'league adjusted' and re-runs a player-for-player trade sees an unchanged verdict labelled as adjusted. They conclude the lens has no effect on trades — or, worse, act on a market-priced equity number believing it is scarcity-corrected. The 291-point gap on this one trade is 7.3% of the equity.

priorFinding.note: Prior stated the overlay scales only rankDerivedValue and named suggestions.py as the mixer. New here: route-level live proof on /api/trade/simulate and /api/trade/finder, the exact 291-point arithmetic gap, and the observation that the honest 'valuationMode' stamp CLAUDE.md is proud of is what turns a silent no-op into an active misstatement.

whatWorks: valuation_mode threading itself is real and correct on all five engine routes I tested: each accepts both the snake_case body field and the camelCase form, each stamps valuationMode on the response, and the finder's top-10 result set genuinely changes between modes (driven by the IDP rows, which DO get repriced).
rootCause: overlay.adjusted_rows repriced the field CLAUDE.md says every engine reads, but two engines read a second field (offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue) for all-offense trades — a case the 'every engine reads exactly one value' invariant does not cover.
requiredRepair: Scale offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue by the same factor inside overlay.adjusted_rows (and audit values.* for the same omission), or have the engines stop preferring the offense-only field when a lens is active. Add a test that asserts an all-offense simulate differs between the two modes.

title: The Next bridge route for /api/trade/suggestions is the only one of four trade/angle bridges that drops the session cookie, so the suggestions feed 401s from the browser
claimUnderTest: The bridge routes exist so the page works without a reverse proxy in front (finder/route.js header comment).
observed: finder/route.js, angle/find/route.js and angle/packages/route.js each read request.headers.get('cookie') and forward it as a Cookie header. suggestions/route.js sends only Content-Type. The identical request that returns HTTP 200 with a full payload against :8000 returns HTTP 401 {'error':'auth_required'} through :3000. Secondary: the suggestions bridge's abort timeout is 5s while the finder's is 30s, even though the backend suggestions call measures 0.04s and the finder 5.48s — the timeouts are on the wrong routes.

reproduction.command: BODY=$(python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print(json.dumps({'roster':d['sleeper']['teams'][0]['players'][:20]}))"); for O in http://127.0.0.1:8000 http://127.0.0.1:3000; do echo -n "$O "; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST $O/api/trade/suggestions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$BODY"; done

numericProof.formula: grep -c Cookie over the four bridge route files

userImpact: Under `npm run dev` and under any deployment where Next serves /api/ directly (as this audit container does), the trade-suggestions panel is permanently signed out. In production nginx routes /api/ to the backend and the bridge is bypassed, so the failure is dev/staging-only — which is exactly why it survives.

priorFinding.note: Prior stated the class ('bridge routes are inconsistent about forwarding the session cookie'); this pins the specific route, the specific status codes, and the three siblings that get it right.

whatWorks: finder, angle/find and angle/packages bridges all forward the cookie correctly and return the backend's status verbatim.
rootCause: Omitted header in one hand-written proxy; no test covers bridge-route cookie forwarding.
requiredRepair: Add `Cookie: request.headers.get('cookie') || ''` to suggestions/route.js. Swap the two abort timeouts. Add one test that asserts every file under frontend/app/api/**/route.js that POSTs to BACKEND_API_URL forwards the cookie header.

title: The finder's 'high confidence' tier is structurally unreachable: it measures the scraper's 3-source site count against a 5-source baseline while the board blends up to 14
claimUnderTest: finder.py: confidence = source_confidence * ktc_confidence with CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE = 5 'Expected source count for full confidence'; _confidence_tier returns 'high' at >= 0.75.
observed: source_count is read from the legacy players dict's _sites field. Across the whole live payload _sites takes only the values 1 (526 rows), 2 (110), 3 (438) and null (18) — the maximum is 3. source_confidence therefore maxes at min(1, 3/5) = 0.60, and with ktc_confidence = 1.0 the confidence score cannot exceed 0.60, one tier below the 0.75 'high' threshold. All 480 returned trades across 12 teams are 'moderate' (244) or 'low' (236); 'high' appears zero times. The board's real blend count is on the contract rows: Brock Bowers has 12 effective post-Hampel sources while his _sites reads 3, and the contract's effectiveSourceRanks distribution runs to 14.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;from collections import Counter;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print('_sites:',Counter(p.get('_sites') for p in d['players'].values()));r=[x for x in d['playersArray'] if x.get('canonicalName')=='Brock Bowers'][0];print('Bowers effectiveSourceRanks:',len(r['effectiveSourceRanks']),'vs _sites:',d['players'][r['legacyRef']]['_sites'])" ; python -c "import json,glob;from collections import Counter;print(Counter(t['confidenceTier'] for f in glob.glob('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W09/finder-*.json') for t in json.load(open(f))['trades']))"
reproduction.actual: _sites max is 3; Bowers effectiveSourceRanks 12 vs _sites 3; Counter({'moderate': 244, 'low': 236})

userImpact: Every arbitrage recommendation on /arbitrage is labelled at most 'moderate confidence', including trades resting on a 12-source consensus. The label is uninformative in one direction and misleadingly pessimistic in the other, and the confidence multiplier (0.7 + 0.3*conf) applies a permanent 0.88 haircut to every score, so it also cannot reorder anything.

priorFinding.note: Prior called the tier 'a constant'. It is not constant — it varies between moderate and low across 480 live trades — but the prior's mechanism claim (it reads the scraper's site count instead of the board's blend count) is exactly right, and the sharper consequence is that the top tier is arithmetically unreachable and the multiplier is a fixed 0.88 for every full-coverage trade.

whatWorks: ktc_confidence and the full/partial coverage distinction are computed correctly; the confidence field is honestly surfaced in the payload rather than hidden.
rootCause: build_asset_pool populates source_count from pdata['_sites'] (the scraper's site count) even on the migrated board path, where the correct quantity is len(row['effectiveSourceRanks']) from the contract.
requiredRepair: Read the blend count from the contract row alongside board_values and positions (a third `source_counts_from_contract` map in the same keying), or lower CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE to match _sites' actual range. The first is correct; the second only hides it.

title: The finder's 'arbitrage' score is 80% own-side gain and 20% opponent appeal, so it ranks lopsidedness rather than the market/board gap it is named for
claimUnderTest: finder.py header: 'Arbitrage score: how much we gain on our board while the opponent sees a fair/favorable deal on KTC.'
observed: Measured over all 480 returned trades: mean f_board_edge = 21.81, mean f_ktc_appeal = 4.95. |boardEdge| accounts for 80.2% of |boardEdge|+|ktcAppeal|. The weights are literal (board_gain_norm*50 vs opp_appeal*30) but the two inputs are not on comparable scales — board_gain_norm routinely exceeds 0.4 on 1-for-2 packages while opp_appeal is gated to be merely positive and averages 0.165. The opponent-appeal term is effectively a pass/fail gate (opp_appeal <= 0 returns None) with a small tiebreaker attached, not half of an arbitrage measure.

reproduction.command: python -c "import json,glob,statistics;c=[t['rankingFactors'] for f in glob.glob('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W09/finder-*.json') for t in json.load(open(f))['trades']];print('mean boardEdge',round(statistics.mean(x['boardEdge'] for x in c),2),'mean ktcAppeal',round(statistics.mean(x['ktcAppeal'] for x in c),2));print('boardEdge share',round(statistics.mean(abs(x['boardEdge'])/(abs(x['boardEdge'])+abs(x['ktcAppeal'])) for x in c)*100,1))"
reproduction.expected: roughly balanced contribution between the two named halves
reproduction.actual: mean boardEdge 21.81, mean ktcAppeal 4.95, boardEdge share 80.2%

userImpact: The top of /arbitrage is ordered by how much the user gains, not by how likely the counterparty is to say yes. A user works the list top-down and gets refused, because the ordering optimises the wrong half of the pitch.

priorFinding.note: Prior claimed 93/7; the live measurement over 480 trades is 80/20. The direction and the mechanism are confirmed; the magnitude differs, which matters because the prior's number would have implied ktcAppeal is nearly inert and it is not.

whatWorks: rankingFactors is a genuinely useful disclosure — every component of the score is stamped per trade, which is what made this measurable at all without instrumenting the engine.
rootCause: Two multipliers (50 and 30) applied to inputs with very different natural ranges, one of which is additionally floor-gated at zero.
requiredRepair: Standardise both terms (e.g. rank-percentile or z-score within the candidate set) before weighting, or state the intended ratio and assert it in a test against a live payload.
dependencies: W09-F002 — the 1-for-2 monoculture is what inflates board_gain_norm in the first place.

title: Finder metadata.myRosterSize reports the post-filter asset count, understating a 57-man roster as 34 and a 44-man roster as 12
claimUnderTest: metadata.myRosterSize alongside assetPoolSize and marketTopNFilter reads as the size of the roster analysed.
observed: my_roster is the output of _resolve_roster against the ALREADY top-N-filtered pool, so myRosterSize is the count of eligible assets, not roster size. Live: Jason 34 reported / 57 rostered, jstuedle 12 / 44, Blaine 16 / 53, Kich 14 / 58. Nothing in the payload carries the true roster size, so a reader cannot recover the coverage ratio — the same information gap that makes W09-F001's empty feed undiagnosable.

reproduction.command: python -c "import json,glob,os;[print(os.path.basename(f)[7:-5], json.load(open(f))['metadata']['myRosterSize']) for f in sorted(glob.glob('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W09/finder-*.json'))]" ; python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print({t['name']:len(t['players']) for t in d['sleeper']['teams']})"
reproduction.actual: Jason 34 vs 57; jstuedle 12 vs 44; Kich 14 vs 58

userImpact: Low direct impact — the field is diagnostic. But it is the one number that would tell an operator the finder is looking at 40% of the roster, and it reports the filtered number as though it were the roster.

priorFinding.note: Prior said a 53-man roster reports as 4. I measure less extreme values (12-34) because the current pool is larger, but the defect is identical.

whatWorks: assetPoolSize (300) and marketTopNFilter (150) are correct and, together with the true roster size, would make the coverage ratio computable.
rootCause: _resolve_roster is called with pool_by_name built from the post-filter pool.
requiredRepair: Stamp both: myRosterSize (from sleeper_teams) and myEligibleAssets (post-filter). One line.

title: No untouchable / excluded-player control exists anywhere in the trade stack — not in the engines, not in the request contracts, not in the UI
claimUnderTest: Prompt section 14 asks whether untouchable/excluded-player controls are wired to candidate generation or only to display filtering.
observed: Neither. A repo-wide search for untouchable / excludePlayer / excludedPlayers / doNotTrade / noTrade across src/, server.py, frontend/app, frontend/components and frontend/lib returns zero hits. find_trades and generate_suggestions_from_pool take no exclusion parameter; /api/trade/finder validates only myTeam, opponentTeams and ktc_top_n; the /arbitrage page has no exclusion UI. The nearest thing is angle/packages' optional `positions` filter and the finder's opponentTeams list, neither of which is per-player. Consequence observed live: the finder recommends Brock Bowers (Jason's #1 asset, board rank 2) in 20 of the 40 trades it returns for Jason, with no way to say 'not him'.

reproduction.command: grep -rn "untouchable\|excludePlayer\|excluded_player\|excludedPlayers\|doNotTrade\|noTrade" src/ server.py frontend/app frontend/components frontend/lib ; echo "exit=$?"

userImpact: A user cannot remove their cornerstone player from consideration, so the top of the recommendation list is dominated by the one asset they will never move, and the genuinely actionable trades are pushed below the 40-result cap.
whatWorks: opponentTeams already demonstrates the pattern for team-level restriction, and angle/packages accepts a positions filter — a per-player exclude list would slot into the same request-validation block.
requiredRepair: Accept `excludePlayers: [name]` on the four POST routes and apply it during candidate generation (drop from my_roster / the pool), not after scoring. Applying it post-hoc would waste the result cap on trades that are then filtered away.

title: The finder performs no dominance pruning: 40 returned trades for Jason are built from only 4 distinct give-side assets, one of which appears in 20 of them
claimUnderTest: _deduplicate 'Remove duplicate trade packages (same assets, different order)' followed by a score sort and a MAX_RESULTS=40 cap.
observed: _deduplicate only collapses exact asset-set repeats. Nothing prunes dominated packages (same give side, strictly worse receive side) and nothing enforces diversity. For Jason, the 40 returned trades draw their give side from 4 distinct players — Brock Bowers 20 times, Jake Golday 11, Andrew Van Ginkel 8, Jalen Redmond 1. The distinct-give-side count across the other 11 teams is comparably narrow. The list is therefore 40 slightly different ways to trade the same handful of players rather than 40 trade ideas.

reproduction.command: python -c "import json;from collections import Counter;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W09/finder-Jason.json'));print(Counter(a['name'] for t in d['trades'] for a in t['give']))"
reproduction.expected: a spread of give-side assets across 40 results
reproduction.actual: Counter({'Brock Bowers': 20, 'Jake Golday': 11, 'Andrew Van Ginkel': 8, 'Jalen Redmond': 1})

userImpact: The user scrolls a 40-row list believing it surveys their trade options; it surveys four of their players. Genuinely different opportunities on the rest of the roster are below the cap and never rendered.

priorFinding.note: Not in the prior index; adjacent to PRIOR-A14-F03 (shape monoculture) but a distinct axis — asset diversity rather than package shape.

whatWorks: _deduplicate does correctly remove genuine permutation duplicates; the defect is that it is the only pruning that runs.
rootCause: No dominance test and no per-asset quota between the sort and the [:max_results] slice.
requiredRepair: Drop packages whose give side is identical and whose receive side is a strict value-subset of a better-scoring package, then cap occurrences per give-side asset (e.g. 3) before slicing to MAX_RESULTS.

title: Trade suggestions emits the same trade under two categories, so totalSuggestions overstates the distinct ideas produced
claimUnderTest: Response separates sellHigh / buyLow / consolidation / positionalUpgrades as distinct suggestion categories with totalSuggestions as their sum.
observed: Brent's feed reports totalSuggestions 9 but contains 7 distinct (give, receive) pairs: 'Rashee Rice -> Jack Campbell' and 'George Pickens -> Carson Schwesinger' each appear in BOTH sellHigh and buyLow with different rationale text. Additionally all 9 suggestions target only two positions (receive-side histogram {LB: 8, QB: 1}), which is the DB-exclusion defect (W09-F004) surfacing in the output.

reproduction.actual: total 9 distinct 7; 2 pairs appear in both sellHigh and buyLow

userImpact: On a feed that already returns 0-9 items for the whole league, presenting the same trade twice under two headings inflates the apparent output by 22% and makes two categories look like corroborating evidence when they are one computation.
whatWorks: Each category's rationale text is genuinely category-specific and correct in isolation ('You have WR surplus (7 rostered, need 4)' vs 'Target Jack Campbell (LB) fills your roster need').
rootCause: sell-high and buy-low search the same surplus/need axes from opposite directions and are not cross-deduplicated before totalSuggestions is summed.
requiredRepair: Deduplicate on (give, receive) across categories, keeping the higher-scoring category and merging the rationale, then recompute totalSuggestions.

title: VERIFIED WORKING: the finder is no longer offense-only — positions_from_contract fixes the per-market gate, IDP assets trade, and the IDP-blindness warning does fire
claimUnderTest: The 2026-08-04 prior audit asserts the finder receives no position data on the live path, is STILL offense-only, and that its own IDP-blindness warning cannot fire. CLAUDE.md asserts the opposite on all three counts plus board_values_from_contract and per-market marketCoverage.
observed: All four CLAUDE.md claims hold on the live path. (1) metadata.valueSource == 'rankDerivedValue' on all 12 team runs, so board_values_from_contract IS the live value source. (2) positions_from_contract populates positions for every row; the gated pool is 300 assets — Counter({DL:70, LB:52, WR:46, RB:31, DB:28, QB:28, PICK:25, TE:20}) — i.e. 150 offense-market + 150 IDP-market, exactly the per-market gate CLAUDE.md describes. (3) IDP assets appear in returned trades for all 12 teams (3 to 40 of the 40 returned per team; 348 of 480 overall). (4) metadata.marketCoverage is emitted per market: {ktcSfTep: 132, ktc: 18, idpTradeCalc: 150}. (5) The IDP-blindness warning is reachable: deleting idpTradeCalc from a deep copy of the players dict makes find_trades emit 'No IDP asset carries an IDPTradeCalc value, so this result is offense-only.' league_has_idp evaluates True from the contract positions and False from the legacy dict alone, which is precisely the bug the fix addressed. Answering the mixed-market question directly: YES, the finder does sum a KTC offense value with an IDPTradeCalc defence value in ktcDelta — 154 of the 480 returned trades — but every such trade stamps marketsUsed: ['idpTradeCalc','ktc'] and mixedMarket: true, and metadata.mixedMarketTrades counts them, so the caveat is disclosed rather than hidden.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/finder -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"myTeam":"Jason","opponentTeams":["all"]}' | python -c "import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);m=r['metadata'];print(m['valueSource'], m['marketCoverage'], m['mixedMarketTrades']);IDP={'DL','LB','DB'};print('trades containing IDP:',sum(1 for t in r['trades'] if any(a['position'] in IDP for a in t['give']+t['receive'])),'of',len(r['trades']))"
reproduction.expected: rankDerivedValue, per-market coverage including a non-zero idpTradeCalc, IDP present in results

numericProof.formula: idpPricedAssets = sum(marketCoverage[k] for k in IDP_MARKET_KEYS)

userImpact: None — this is a verified negative. Recording it so the prior audit's Critical F-00/F-01 are not carried forward into a repair plan.

priorFinding.note: Also refutes PRIOR-A14-F01 (warning cannot fire — I made it fire), PRIOR-A14-F14 (fits ' ' need on an empty position string — the live rationale reads 'sheds DL surplus, fills DB need'), PRIOR-A14-F02 (finder applies KTC's Value Adjustment to the market side only — the current finder.py imports no VA at all; angle.py applies _adjusted_pair_totals symmetrically to BOTH my-values and market-values at lines 778 and 798), and PRIOR-A14-F20 in part (of the three CLAUDE.md claims it disputes, the per-market gate and the IDP warning are correct; only the assetsUnpricedByBoard number differs — live is 186, the docstring says 189/202). The prior audit's evidence was code reading; the live path disagrees with it.

whatWorks: The whole per-market anchoring design. Ranking each market's own population from 1 is also the exact fix W09-F004 needs in suggestions.py.

title: The partner-fit / acceptance model is rigorous and honest about its own unidentifiability, and no page in the product can reach it
claimUnderTest: Prompt section 15: with only 12 managers there is little behavioural history — is manager-specific history shrunk toward a prior, does any output claim a manager WILL accept, is sample size visible?
observed: The model answers all three correctly, on a live call. Manager-specific history is not merely shrunk, it is REFUSED: managerEvidence.admissible is false for all 11 partners with the reason 'no decision data: the league snapshot records only completed trades, so rejections are unobserved and an acceptance rate is unidentifiable. Manager-specific term contributes zero', and contributions.managerSpecific is 0.0 for every partner. Sample size is explicit (decisionsObserved 0, acceptsObserved 0, rejectsObserved 0). Nothing claims acceptance: the field is named tradeAcceptanceEstimate, ships beside acceptanceConfidence capped at 0.255 (declared ceiling 0.4 without rejection data), carries evidence: 'shapeOnly', and a note stating it 'is a plausibility score in probability units, not a calibrated acceptance probability'. The contributions breakdown is fully itemised (prior -1.5163, rosterFit -0.5274, windowFit 0.3935, everything else 0.0). THE DEFECT IS REACH: /api/gameplan is the only route serving it, it has no Next bridge route (404 via :3000), and grep across frontend/app, frontend/components and frontend/lib finds zero references to gameplan, tradePartnerFitScore, acceptanceConfidence or partnerNeedAlignment. The best-calibrated uncertainty disclosure in this codebase is unreachable by a user.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/gameplan?team=468418790212759552' | python -c "import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);p=r['partners'][0];print(p['acceptanceConfidence'], p['evidence'], p['managerEvidence']['decisionsObserved'], p['contributions'])" ; curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'bridge=%{http_code}\n' -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/gameplan ; grep -rn 'tradePartnerFitScore\|acceptanceConfidence\|gameplan' frontend/app frontend/components frontend/lib | grep -v node_modules
reproduction.actual: 0.255 shapeOnly 0 {'leagueHistory': 0.0, 'managerSpecific': 0.0, 'marketFairness': 0.0, 'prior': -1.5163, 'rosterFit': -0.5274, 'windowFit': 0.3935}; bridge=404; the only frontend match is frontend/app/api/valuation/league-adjusted/route.js, which uses gameplan for factors, not partners

numericProof.formula: observed max tradePartnerFitScore vs declared reachable max

userImpact: Users get acceptance-flavoured guidance from other surfaces with none of this discipline, while the surface that would have told them 'this is a plausibility score, not a probability, and we have zero decision observations' is not rendered anywhere.

priorFinding.note: Prior stated the reachable range [7.24, 43.12] is unreachable through the only wiring that serves it, with a measured live ceiling of 16.x. I measure exactly 16.0 as the maximum across 11 partners (range 10.76-16.0), so the declared max is 2.7x the observed one. Also confirms PRIOR-A10-F15 in part (authoritative docstrings, no production consumer) for this module specifically.

whatWorks: Nearly everything about the model itself: the refusal to estimate from accepts-only data, the confidence ceiling tied to evidence rather than to the partner, the per-term contributions breakdown, the five explanatory notes per partner, the modelVersion stamp, and the limitations block with explicit canSupport / cannotSupport / keyAssumptions including which assumptions are measured and which are not. This is the standard the rest of the trade stack should be held to.
rootCause: No page and no bridge route were built for /api/gameplan.
requiredRepair: Either render partners on /trade or /arbitrage (with acceptanceConfidence and managerEvidence.decisionsObserved shown, not just the score), or narrow the declared tradePartnerFitScoreRange to what the live wiring can produce so the declared range stops describing a configuration that does not exist.

title: Monte Carlo run-to-run variance is small but no convergence statistic is exposed, and the panel that calls it 404s through the Next origin
claimUnderTest: Prompt section 15: run simulate-mc 10 times on the same input and measure variance; is convergence exposed; does simulate disagree with simulate-mc?
observed: Variance is genuinely low — 10 identical calls give meanDelta in [-4455.2, -4439.3] (population sd 5.13 on a magnitude of 4,447, i.e. 0.12%), stdDelta in [1439.3, 1449.6], winProbA in [0.0001, 0.0003]. But no convergence statistic, standard error, confidence interval or seed echo is returned, so a caller cannot distinguish a stable 0.50 from a noisy one; the only diagnostic is symmetryCheck.drift, which measures ordering bias, not convergence. nSims is also reported as double the request (asked 50000, got 100000) because symmetrize sums the two directional passes (symmetrize.py:74) — the UI renders that as 'X% of 100,000 simulations'. simulate and simulate-mc do NOT disagree on value source: both prefer offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue for all-offense trades and agree at 4004 / -3945 respectively once the same inputs are used (the 59-point gap is entirely explained by the frontend sending effectiveValue while the backend simulate reads the row). Separately, POST /api/trade/simulate-mc and /api/trade/simulate return 404 through http://127.0.0.1:3000, which is the origin the page is served from — MonteCarloButton fetches the relative path, so the panel is dead outside a reverse-proxied deployment.

reproduction.command: for i in $(seq 10); do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sideA":[{"name":"Brock Bowers","rankDerivedValue":9947,"pos":"TE","team":"LV"}],"sideB":[{"name":"Jonathan Taylor","rankDerivedValue":6431,"pos":"RB","team":"IND"},{"name":"Patrick Mahomes","rankDerivedValue":7461,"pos":"QB","team":"KC"}]}' | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["meanDelta"], r["winProbA"], r["nSims"])'; done ; curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'next-origin simulate-mc=%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
reproduction.expected: a convergence/SE field, nSims matching the request, and a reachable route from the page origin
reproduction.actual: meanDelta spread 15.9 over 10 runs; no SE/CI/seed field; nSims 100000 for a 50000 request; next-origin simulate-mc=404

userImpact: A user cannot tell whether a 50/50 result is a genuine coin flip or sampling noise, and the sim count quoted in the plain-English summary is twice what was requested. In any deployment where Next serves /api/ (dev, and this audit container), the button errors out.

priorFinding.note: The missing-bridge-route half is exactly PRIOR-A14-F23, verified live (404 on both simulate and simulate-mc through :3000 while finder/angle bridges answer). The convergence-exposure and nSims-doubling observations are new. I could NOT reproduce PRIOR-A14-F06's claim that the frontend strips the disclaimer in a way that makes the result unreadable — the backend does return labelHint + disclaimer, and MonteCarloButton does substitute its own plain-English text; whether that violates the contract is a judgement call I am recording as partial rather than confirmed.

whatWorks: The estimator is stable and the symmetrization is real and verified (drift 0.0001, enforced true). The 503 feature-disabled path is clean.
rootCause: No SE computation in monte_carlo.py; nSims summed across the two symmetrization passes; no route.js under frontend/app/api/trade/simulate*.
requiredRepair: Return mcStandardError = sqrt(p*(1-p)/nSims) on winProbA and echo the seed. Report nSims as requested (or rename to nDraws). Add the two bridge routes, forwarding the cookie.
dependencies: W09-F005 — a convergence statistic on a fabricated distribution still describes the wrong quantity.
